title: Quarto skills presentation
text:
Preface
Quarto is an open-source publishing tool that turns a single source file into professional documents, presentations, and websites. It allows you to write your content once, and instantly export it to HTML, PDF, or Microsoft Word.
This book is a collection of notes and examples that I have found useful when using Quarto. It is not intended to be a comprehensive guide, but rather a reference for myself and others who are learning to use this tool. This book itself is written in Quarto, and you can find the source code on GitHub.

title: Installation
section: Add some code to your document
text:
Add some code to your document
To add a python code block to your Quarto document, you can use code blocks like this:
# My First Quarto Document
This is a simple Quarto document

```{python}
print(3+3)
```
Now you can try rendering the document again using the same command:
quarto preview my_notes.qmd
You will notice an error like:
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'
Python 3 installation:
{}

Jupyter is not available in this Python installation. 
Install with python3 -m pip install jupyter
When you render a Quarto document containing Python code blocks, Quarto needs an “engine” to execute the code and capture the results to insert into the final document, for this reason, Quarto requires Jupyter to be installed in your Python environment. You can do this by installing Jupyter in your Python environment. So, first create and activate a virtual environment with:
python3 -m venv myenv
source myenv/bin/activate






NoteWindows users





Windows users can activate the virtual environment in PowerShell with:
myenv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
or in Command Prompt (cmd) with:
myenv\Scripts\activate.bat



and then install Jupyter with:
python3 -m pip install jupyter
and then try rendering the document again using the same command:
quarto preview my_notes.qmd

title: Installation
text:
Python and Jupyter
Quarto uses Jupyter to execute Python code blocks and capture their output. Create a virtual environment and install Jupyter into it:
python3 -m venv myenv
source myenv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install jupyter






NoteWindows users





Activate the virtual environment in PowerShell with:
myenv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
or in Command Prompt with:
myenv\Scripts\activate.bat
Then install Jupyter the same way: python3 -m pip install jupyter

title: Installation
text:
Adding Python code
To include executable Python code, use a {python} code block:
# My First Quarto Document
This is a simple Quarto document

```{python}
print(3+3)
```
Save the file — the preview will refresh automatically and display the output below the code block.
